_comment: An EMPTY enum override. An enum that admits nothing is a typo, not a request, so the
config decoder rejects it — the same policy as the unknown scalar kind beside it.
It was harmless before only by accident: `AEnumMap []` matched nothing in the phantom
emitters and fell through to a plain `String` setter, i.e. it was swallowed by the very
bug that made every enum override a no-op. Now that an all-identity override IS an
`AEnum`, an empty one would mint `type alias Strict = {}` and a `Value {}` setter that
no token can satisfy — dead code, emitted in silence.
This fixture also pins the arm that made the rejection REACHABLE. `Generate.elm` used
to answer a config decode error by falling back to the raw manifest declarations,
which discarded the entire legacy front-end (`_exclude`, every `attrTypes` override,
every synthetic attr) from one typo, with a zero exit code and no diagnostic. Every
fail-loud branch in the config decoder returned an `Err` that arm threw away.
